question: I want to prepare a standard sodium carbonate solution using this lab setup. Please guide me through the steps as they happen.
event: I want to prepare a standard sodium carbonate solution using this lab setup. Please guide me through the steps as they happen.

ground_truth.response: Carefully transfer the weighed sodium carbonate powder from the watch glass into the glass beaker. Use the stirring rod to help guide all the powder into the beaker.
Add about 50 ml of distilled water to the beaker using the wash bottle to begin dissolving the powder. Use the stream to rinse the beaker walls.
Now, carefully pour the dissolved sodium carbonate solution from the beaker into the 250 ml volumetric flask. Ensure you don't spill any liquid during the transfer.
Continue filling the flask with distilled water. Watch the graduation mark on the neck closely; this indicates your final target volume of 250 ml.
Finally, place the glass stopper on the flask and invert it several times to mix the solution thoroughly until it is completely homogeneous.

Position the poles over the tent and insert the ends into the metal grommets at each corner. Then, snap the plastic clips of the inner tent onto the poles.

question: I'm following along with this tutorial to learn how to prepare a mango. Please give me step-by-step instructions as the process unfolds.
event: I'm following along with this tutorial to learn how to prepare a mango. Please give me step-by-step instructions as the process unfolds.

ground_truth.response: Position the butter knife near the stem and use a sawing motion to cut off a large cheek. Feel for the central seed to guide your blade.
Score the mango flesh with vertical and horizontal cuts to create a grid pattern. Be careful not to pierce through the outer skin.
Press the skin from the back to invert the piece, making the mango cubes pop outward for easy access.
Flip the mango over and repeat the sawing motion to remove the second large cheek from the other side of the seed.
Score this second cheek as well. You can use diagonal cuts this time for a different aesthetic if you prefer.
Saw off the thinner strips of fruit remaining around the central seed to salvage all the edible parts.
ground_truth.event_description: Removing side pieces from the seed

ground_truth.response: Next, cut those smaller side pieces you removed into bite-sized chunks to make them easier to eat.
